intro: A sampled action receives a signed advantage. The score-function gradient shifts probability toward helpful actions and away from harmful ones while balancing each row.
task: Compute the negative mean advantage-weighted log-probability loss and its gradient with respect to the supplied logits.
requirements: logits is a nonempty (B,A) matrix. actions is a vector of B integer-valued category indices in [0,A). advantages has length B and may contain positive, zero, or negative values.
Treat advantages as fixed supplied weights. The gradient is for minimizing the stated negative objective, not for gradient ascent. Do not normalize advantages or take another mean over actions.

Use real finite numeric inputs of magnitude at most 1e30, excluding boolean parameters. Vectors have 1..256 entries and each matrix axis has length 1..256 unless a stricter bound is stated. Leave caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Differentiate one selected log-probability
hints.body: The derivative is one_hot(action)-probability before the negative-loss sign.

hints.title: Check the sum over actions
hints.body: Each row of the logit gradient sums to zero, reflecting invariance to a common logit shift.

explanation: A positive advantage makes gradient descent increase the chosen action logit relative to the others. A negative advantage reverses that direction.
This explicit derivative is a small score-function calculation from supplied samples. Estimating useful advantages and collecting rollouts are separate parts of policy optimization.
